canonical_definition: Visual Understanding refers to the ability to extract, integrate, and reason about visual information from images at multiple levels (image-, object-, pixel-level) to support tasks such as question answering, captioning, commonsense reasoning, and planning. It encompasses recognizing objects, localizing regions, interpreting fine-grained details, and aligning visual content with language, often operationalized through vision-language alignment, multi-layer visual features, or enhanced tokenization. Some definitions emphasize specific applications (e.g., 3D consistency detection, robotic action parsing) or training strategies (e.g., visual instruction tuning), but core to all is the integration of localized and global visual context for downstream reasoning.
